title: Cities in Singapore: Top Areas You Must Explore
summary: Discover the top cities in Singapore and unique districts worth exploring. From Marina Bay to Jurong, find out what makes each area special.
body_markdown:
[Singapore](https://blog.transfez.com/en/living-abroad/singapore/)


Singapore is tiny. Like, really tiny. You can drive from one end to the other in under an hour. Yet somehow, this little island packs in more personality, culture, and jaw-dropping sights than countries ten times its size. If you are planning a visit, a move, or even just dreaming about life there, knowing the different cities and districts in Singapore can completely change how you experience the place. And if you are thinking about[working abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/working-abroad-complete-beginners-guide/) for the first time, Singapore is one of the most popular destinations Indonesians choose, so understanding its layout is genuinely useful.


Here is the thing though. Singapore does not have “cities” in the traditional sense. It is a city-state, meaning the entire country is essentially one city. But within that city, there are very distinct towns, planning areas, and districts that each feel like their own little world. Let us break them down.

##


**What Are the Main Cities and Districts in Singapore?**


Singapore is divided into five main regions: Central, North, North-East, East, and West. Within those regions, you will find around 55 planning areas, each with its own vibe, architecture, food scene, and purpose. Below are the most important ones you should know about.


###


**1. Marina Bay and the Central Business District (CBD)**


This is the postcard version of Singapore. The glittering Marina Bay Sands, the Gardens by the Bay supertrees, and the sleek glass towers of the CBD all cluster together here. It is where finance, tourism, and architecture collide in the most spectacular way possible.


If you are working in banking, tech, or multinational firms, there is a good chance your office will be somewhere in this zone. It is polished, walkable, and absolutely stunning at night.


###


**2. Orchard Road**


Think of Orchard Road as Singapore’s answer to Paris’s Champs-Elysees, but with more air conditioning. This is the shopping belt of Singapore, lined with malls, flagship stores, hotels, and restaurants stretching for about 2.2 kilometers.


Beyond shopping, Orchard is a key residential and diplomatic zone. Many embassies and luxury condominiums sit just off the main strip.


###


**3. Chinatown**


Do not let the name fool you. Yes, Chinatown in Singapore is rich with Chinese heritage, red lanterns, and traditional shophouses. But it is also one of the most cosmopolitan neighborhoods on the island, where you will find incredible hawker food, buzzing nightlife, and a mix of cultures all rubbing shoulders.


The Maxwell Food Centre here is legendary. If you visit only one hawker centre in Singapore, make it this one.


###


**4. Little India**


Step into Little India and your senses go into overdrive, in the best way. Fragrant flower garlands, colorful sari shops, the sound of Tamil music drifting from doorways, and the smell of freshly made roti prata. This district is a living, breathing celebration of Indian culture and has been for over 150 years.


It is also home to the Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple, one of the most visually stunning religious sites in Singapore.


###


**5. Kampong Glam**


This is Singapore’s Malay and Arab quarter, centered around the iconic Sultan Mosque with its golden dome. The streets around here, especially Haji Lane, have transformed into a hip, creative district packed with independent boutiques, vintage shops, and specialty cafes.


It is the kind of area where old-world charm and modern cool exist side by side without any awkwardness.


##


**Residential Towns Worth Knowing in Singapore**


Beyond the tourist-heavy districts, Singapore has a network of well-planned residential towns that are home to the majority of Singaporeans and expats. These are often called *new towns* and they are worth understanding, especially if you are considering living or working there.


###


**1. Jurong East and Jurong West**


Located in the western part of Singapore, the Jurong region has grown from an industrial hub into a fully-fledged urban center. Jurong East in particular is being developed as Singapore’s second CBD, with massive commercial, retail, and residential projects underway.


For people[working in Singapore](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-work-in-singapore/) in manufacturing, logistics, or engineering, Jurong is often where life happens.


###


**2. Tampines**


Tampines is one of Singapore’s most mature and well-loved residential towns. Located in the East, it has great transport links, plenty of malls, parks, and a strong community feel. Many Indonesian professionals and students settle in the East region because of its accessibility.


###


**3. Woodlands**


Sitting right at the northern tip of Singapore, Woodlands is just across the causeway from Johor Bahru in Malaysia. This makes it a popular base for people who commute between the two countries. It is affordable, green, and increasingly well-connected thanks to ongoing development.


###


**4. Punggol**


Punggol is Singapore’s youngest and most futuristic new town. Built around a waterway and designed as a smart, eco-friendly community, it attracts young families and professionals. If you want a glimpse of where Singapore is heading, Punggol is it.


###


**5. Buona Vista and One-North**


This western district is Singapore’s innovation and research hub. One-North is home to biomedical companies, tech startups, media firms, and universities. If you are in the sciences, tech, or creative industries, this area will likely be on your radar.


##


**Singapore’s Cultural and Lifestyle Enclaves**


Some parts of Singapore do not fit neatly into the “residential” or “commercial” boxes. They are more about lifestyle, heritage, and character, and they are absolutely worth exploring.


###


**1. Tiong Bahru**


Tiong Bahru is arguably Singapore’s coolest neighborhood. It combines pre-war *Art Deco* architecture with a thriving cafe culture, independent bookshops, and gourmet food spots. Morning dim sum next to artisan coffee? Yes, that is Tiong Bahru.


###


**2. Holland Village**


Long a favorite of expats, Holland Village is a laid-back enclave with a European-village feel. Great restaurants, weekend markets, and a relaxed atmosphere make it a beloved spot for both locals and foreigners settling into Singapore life.


If you are navigating the experience of[living abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/living-abroad-tips/) for the first time, neighborhoods like Holland Village can feel like a soft landing, familiar enough to feel comfortable, new enough to feel exciting.


###


**3. Sentosa Island**


Technically connected to the mainland by a causeway, Sentosa is Singapore’s leisure island. Universal Studios, beach clubs, cable cars, and luxury resorts all call this place home. It is touristy, yes, but also genuinely fun.


##


**Why Knowing Singapore’s Districts Matters for Indonesians**


Singapore is the number one destination for[the Indonesian diaspora](https://blog.transfez.com/en/indonesian-diaspora-who-they-are-and-why-they-matter/) in Southeast Asia. Whether you are going for a job, an internship, or further studies, knowing which district suits your lifestyle, budget, and commute can save you a lot of stress when you first arrive.


Each area has a different energy, a different cost of living, and different access to transport and amenities. Do your research before you commit to a neighborhood, and do not just go by what looks pretty on Instagram.

Singapore may be small, but its districts are big on personality. Whether you are drawn to the gleaming towers of Marina Bay, the cultural richness of Kampong Glam, or the chill vibes of Tiong Bahru, there is a corner of Singapore that will feel like it was made for you.
